events.title: The death of St. Ignatius of Loyola
events.shortBlurb: The founder of the Society of Jesus died at Rome as his young order spread across the world…
body: In his last years Ignatius lived quietly at Rome, governing by letter a Society that in sixteen years had grown from ten companions to about a thousand members on both sides of the Atlantic. At the urging of his sons he dictated the story of his conversion to Father Luis Goncalves da Camara, the plain account since known as his Autobiography.

In the summer of 1556 he was seized by Roman fever. On 30 July he sent his secretary Polanco to beg a last blessing of Pope Paul IV, but the physicians saw no danger and the errand was put off till morning. At dawn on 31 July he was found peacefully dying, and he passed before the holy oils could be brought.

He was buried at Santa Maria della Strada, where now the Gesu stands and his tomb is venerated. Diego Lainez was chosen to succeed him as general. Beatified by Paul V in 1609, Ignatius was canonized by Gregory XV in 1622, in the same ceremony as Francis Xavier and Teresa of Avila.
